title: Vessels and garments: why the letters are called both
overview:
Chapter 39 asks why the letters are called both *kelim* (vessels) and *levushim* (garments). They are vessels because they are born with the idea and make it what it is: limit and define it as they may, they are counted with the essence, as organs are part of the body. A vessel is not a pot that holds the soup: spill the soup and it is still soup, but lose the letters of an idea and the idea is gone. Their root, the *chomer hapashut*, even comes before the lights.

They are also garments: once they exist, the idea hides in them as if it could only be this way, and yet it can put on other combinations, which is why two commentators say one idea in two ways, and why a worry or a will goes through thought after thought. A book's letters can be cut up or burned, but change one and it is another book. Both are true because the letters' root in the Essence is higher than light. Rabbi Markel says the whole book depends on this: the worlds, the *kelipos*, *Tohu*, and the princes of the nations.

terms.gloss: vessels; really like organs, part of the essence and what makes a thing what it is, not like a pot
garments; separate from the essence, which dresses in them, hides in them and can change them
letters; the form in which an idea, a will or a feeling comes out and is what it is
a line of reasoning; the minute it comes out of the power of insight, it comes out with letters
the power that brings insight, from which the idea comes out
combinations of letters; one idea can be revealed in different ones
the simple matter of the Atzmus: the root of the vessels, before the lights, that even the original light is made of
the Oral Torah; a hybrid, where one idea can be said in different ways and both are Torah
a husk or peel; the outside of the letters peeled off, a garment no longer connected
the princes of the seventy nations: the letters, will and power of insight of a country, higher than the shedim
demons; the personal daemon of an individual, with three levels, Chabad, Chagas and Nehi

sections.title: Letters as vessels: born with the idea and counted with the essence
sections.summary: The letters of the intellect, the will and the *middos* come out together with the thing itself and make it what it is. Though they limit and define it, they are counted with the essence, as organs are part of the body: this is what is called *kelim*.

phrases.he: (לט) ומעתה יובן דרך כלל במה שהאותיות נקראים כלים וגם נקראים לבושים
כי לכאורה בחינת הכלי הוא נחשב מן העצם, גם שהוא המגביל לעצם
כמו אותיות הקבועים תמיד בעצם הנפש, שמתאחדים עם העצם
על דרך דוגמא מאותיות החקוקים בציור או בבליטה, כאותיות החותם
כך ברוחניות האותיות דנפש
וכמו גלוי עצם החי בכח התנועה, או כגלוי חיות המתפשת מעצם החי, שקבוע כח זה בהעלם בעצמו כו'
וכמו שאנו רואים באותיות השכל
הכלולים בעצם כח השכל
שמיד שיוציא לאור הסברא מכח המשכיל שלו, יצאו עמה אותיות
phrases.en: The minute the *sevara* comes out of the *koach hamaskil*, it comes out with letters.

phrases.he: שבהם ועל ידם אופן מציאת ישותו בדבר מה,
phrases.en: And through the letters is the way that this *sechel* that comes out has an existence of a something in a way of what it is.

phrases.he: והוא אותיות כל השכלה לכל מי שימציאנה
phrases.en: And this is the letters of any *haskala* no matter who discovers it.

blocks.text: Why are the letters called both *kelim* (vessels) and *levushim* (garments)? The vessel is counted with the *etzem* (essence) though it limits it, like a seal's engraved letters, the power of movement, or the letters of the intellect: these are all *kelim*. The minute the *sevara* (line of reasoning) comes out of the *koach hamaskil* (the power that brings insight), **it comes out with letters**. What makes the idea this idea is its letters, and they are **the letters of any *haskala* no matter who discovers it**.

phrases.he: וראיה מב' בני אדם בהשכלתם שכל וסברא אחד זה יוציאנה באותיות וצרופים כאלה וזה יוציאנה בגלוי באופני אותיות וצרופים אחרים
phrases.en: Two people who will explain the same thing: one will bring it out in one set of letters, and one will bring it out in another set of letters.

phrases.he: (כפרושי המפרשים לתלמוד, מסבירים לשכל וסברא אחד
בפירוש רש''י ופירוש התוספות ורא''ש ור''ן, וכהאי גוונא, בלשונות מיוחדים, והכל עולה לענין ומכוין אחד,
רק שכל אחד מפרש באותיות שכל שלו כו',
phrases.en: Each one says in a totally different way.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר)
כי בהולד גוף השכל יולדו עמו אותיות שלו שנראה בהן בבחינת יש,
phrases.en: When the *guf* of a *haskala* is born its letters are born with it, and through these letters it is seen into what it is, its somethingness.

phrases.he: ואף על פי שמתארו ומגבילו,
phrases.en: Even though these letters describe it and limit it, define it,

phrases.he: מכל מקום נחשב עם העצם כו'
phrases.en: nonetheless, they're really part of the *etzem* of the *sechel* itself.

blocks.text: The proof: of two people with one idea, **one will bring it out in one set of letters**, the other in another. So Rashi, Tosafos, the Rosh and the Ran explain one idea, each in his own language. Not where they disagree: where they *mamash* (actually) agree, **each one says in a totally different way**.

When the *guf* (body) of an idea is born, its letters are born with it, and through them it is seen as what it is, its somethingness. **Even though these letters describe it and limit it**, they are **really part of the *etzem* of the *sechel* itself**.

phrases.he: וכן אותיות הרצון
phrases.en: Same thing with the letters of the *ratzon*,

phrases.he: ואותיות המדות כמו אהבה בלב
שתתגלה בבחינת אותיות שלה,
phrases.en: that it's revealed in its letters,

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת אופן גלויה במציאות בכמה אופנים שונים,
phrases.en: that this is how it is revealed in revelation in several different ways,

phrases.he: כמו שכל אחד שמתגלה בצירופים שונים כו'
phrases.en: in the same way, like one *sechel* that is revealed in varied *tzirufim*.

phrases.he: וזהו הנקרא בחינת כלים, שהוא בחינת היש המתאר ומגביל, ונחשב עם העצם
כמו כל בחינת כלים דעשר ספירות, כלי האור דחכמה וכלי האור דחסד ונצח וכהאי גוונא,
שהוא בחינת היש והתואר שלהם כו', כידוע
phrases.en: This is the somethingness and the description of this *sefira* as its letters.

blocks.text: **Same thing with the letters of the *ratzon***: they are part of the *etzem* of the will, its *kelim*. So with the letters of the *middos* (emotional attributes), like love in the heart: **it's revealed in its letters**, in several different ways, as one idea is revealed in different *tzirufim* (combinations of letters).

This is what is called *kelim*: the somethingness that describes and limits and is counted with the essence, like the vessels of the ten *sefiros*, the vessel of the light of *chachma* and of *chesed*. In the body they are called organs. The *kelim* are like organs and the *levushim* like clothing: the organs are part of the *etzem*, and the clothing is not.

sections.title: The root of the vessels comes before the lights: an organ, not a pot
sections.summary: The vessel is made from the thickening of the light, and yet its root, the *chomer hapashut*, comes before the lights. A *kli* is not a pot that holds soup: it is an organ like the eye, without which the thing cannot be what it is.

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב באות כ''ח שמהתעבות האור נעשה כלי
phrases.en: The *kli* comes from the thickening up of the light.

phrases.he: וגם שרש הכלים קדם לאורות,
phrases.en: Not only that, but the root of the *kelim* preceded the lights.

phrases.he: שנקרא חומר הפשוט כו'
phrases.en: That is called the simple *chomer* of the *Atzmus*.

phrases.he: וכמובן מהנזכר לעיל בהאותיות שבעצם הנפש, קדם לשרש התהוות אור עצם הרצון והתענוג כו')
phrases.en: The letters in *etzem hanefesh* preceded the actual light of the *etzem haratzon v'taanug*.

blocks.text: **The *kli* comes from the thickening up of the light**, and yet **the root of the *kelim* preceded the lights**, as the letters come before even the *ratzon hapashut* (the simple will): for a light to come out, there had to be the description of what it is. That root is **the simple *chomer* of the *Atzmus*** (G-d's essence), as the soul's letters come before its will and delight.

blocks.title: The pot and the soup
blocks.text: That is why they are called *kelim*, and really like organs. People usually think *kelim* means vessels, like a pot. But a pot is not part of the *etzem*; it is really a *levush*. It holds the soup in, but it is not what makes it soup. Take away the pot and you still have soup, spilled all over the floor and perfectly edible: a dog will come and lick it right up. The only reason you care is that the floor is dirty. Taking away the *kli* did not take away what it is. The real *kli* is an organ, like the eye a listener spoke of, which is part of the *etzem* of seeing.

The letters of the intellect are not like the pot. Lose them and you cannot think the idea at all; it is lost. Without the eye, the light of the eye is still there, but you cannot see. And the light itself has *kelim*: though *kelim* come from the thickening of the lights, there is a *kli* before the whole thing that made it what it is, the *chomer hapashut* that even the original light is made of.

sections.title: Letters as garments: the essence hides in them, and can change them
sections.summary: Once the letters exist, the idea hides in them as a body in clothing, as if it could only be this way. Really it can take off one set of combinations and put on another; the letters never reach its essence, which is why two people say one idea in two ways.

phrases.he: אך עם כל זה גם זה אמת, שהאותיות נקראים גם כן בשם לבושים
כי הנה בחינת הלבוש הוא דבר נבדל מן העצם לגמרי
phrases.en: It's really a totally different thing,

phrases.he: רק שבו מתלבש העצם, כמו שהגוף מתלבש בלבוש זר ונבדל מעצמו, ומכסהו ומעלימו
כך האותיות של השכל, אחר התהוותן במציאותן הרי העצם של השכל מתלבש ומתעלם בהם,
כי לא נגלה רק בחינת אותיות של השכל, שהוא אופן ישותו כו',
phrases.en: only the way it is,

phrases.he: כאילו אין דבר חוץ מאופן זה
phrases.en: as if there's no other way.

blocks.text: And yet it is also true that the letters are called *levushim*. A garment is **really a totally different thing**, which the essence only dresses in, as the body dresses in clothing that covers and hides it. So the letters of the intellect, once they exist: the essence of the idea hides in them, and all that shows is **only the way it is**, **as if there's no other way**, as if it has to be *davka* (precisely) this way.

phrases.he: ובאמת עצם אור השכל הזה איננו מובדל באופן כזה דוקא
phrases.en: It's not really *davka* in this way.

phrases.he: כי כמו לבוש יחליף ויתלבש באופני צירופים שונים אחרים לגמרי
phrases.en: It can take off this whole *levush*, and will be *mislabesh* in a whole different *tzirufim*, the same *sechel*.

phrases.he: וכללם אינם מגיעים בעצם מהותו כלל, רק שבהן מתלבש ומתגלה
phrases.en: And really the *tzirufim* don't really get to the *etzem mahus* of the *sechel*; it's only that in these *tzirufim* it is *mislabesh*, and that's how it's revealed.

phrases.he: (על דרך הנזכר לעיל באופני גלוי שכל וסברא אחד בלשונות המפרשים כו')

blocks.text: But the light of the intellect is **not really *davka* in this way**. Like a garment, **it can take off this whole *levush*, and will be *mislabesh* in a whole different *tzirufim***, and it is the same idea. The combinations never reach what it is in itself; it only dresses, and shows itself, in them.

This is *mamash* the same *mashal* (analogy) used before to show that the letters are *kelim*; now it shows they are *levushim*. Two people tell you the same idea in two different ways. Were the letters the very essence of the idea, everybody would have to say it exactly the same way.

sections.title: Will and thought change their garments every moment
sections.summary: One simple will dresses itself in many ways of showing itself, and a feeling of the heart dresses in thought after thought, as a body changes clothes. So does the intellect, once it comes into the letters of thought.

phrases.he: וכך הוא באותיות הרצון,
phrases.en: And same thing with *osios haratzon*.

phrases.he: שהרי רצון אחד פשוט מתלבש בכמה מיני גלויי אופנים שונים
ואינו רק רצון אחד,
phrases.en: It's really just one *ratzon*.

phrases.he: וכמו בלבוש יתלבש הגוף
phrases.en: The same like the body will enclose itself in a *levush*,

phrases.he: כך הרצון בא באופן גלוי שלו להחליף תמיד כו'
phrases.en: the *ratzon* comes in a way of a *levush*, and it always changes it.

blocks.text: **Same thing with *osios haratzon*** (the letters of the will). One simple will dresses itself in many different ways of showing itself, and **it's really just one *ratzon***. As a body dresses in clothing, **the *ratzon* comes in a way of a *levush*, and it always changes it**: the thought keeps changing.

phrases.he: וכמו שאנו רואים באותיות המחשבה המלבישים למדות
שהאהבה שבלב שכבר באה באופן אותיות הגלוי שלה בלב, הנה בבואה במחשבה, הרי היא מתלבשת שם במחשבה זאת, כגוף שמתלבש בלבוש נפרד ממש
שעל זה אמר כלבוש תחליפם ממש
phrases.en: You'll change them like a *levush*.

phrases.he: שהרי לבוש המחשבה אינו עומד אפילו רגע,
phrases.en: The *levush* of *machshava* doesn't stand even for one second.

phrases.he: שתמיד פושט ולובש ופושט ולובש כו' ממחשבה למחשבה כו'
phrases.en: Every second it goes from one *machshava* to another *machshava*.

blocks.title: The worrier
blocks.text: Love in the heart dresses itself in thought like a body in a garment *mamash* separate from it, and the thoughts change every second. A man sitting and worrying does not repeat "I'm worried, I'm worried" like a mantra. He thinks: what's the other fellow going to say? What will I say? It is one *midda* dressed in different thoughts, put on and taken off.

That is why it says **you'll change them like a *levush***. **The *levush* of *machshava* doesn't stand even for one second**. It does not stay with one thought, like the worry said over and over: **every second it goes from one *machshava* to another *machshava***.

phrases.he: וכך גם אור השכל בבואו בלבוש דאותיות המחשבה, ממש פושט ולובש ממחשבה למחשבה כו'

blocks.text: So too the light of the intellect in the garment of the letters of thought: it takes them off and puts them on. Thinking an idea over, you do not sit and think exactly the same words, even the words of this book, over and over like memorization. So the garment is not part of it.

sections.title: Which letters are vessels and which are garments: the book and the Torah scroll
sections.summary: The letters of the intellect in the essence look just like garments. A book's letters can be cut up or burned, yet change one and it is another book: the written letters are garments that must fit the vessels, and the vessels, the idea's own letters, cannot be destroyed.

phrases.he: (מה שאין כן בחינת גלוי אותיות השכל בעצם הנזכר לעיל,
שנחשב עם העצם
רק שנראה כמו לבוש דאותיות המחשבה ממש
phrases.en: But it looks like the same like *levush*, it's hard to tell the difference.

phrases.he: אחר התהוותן במציאת נבדל מן עצם השכל כו', כנזכר לעיל)

blocks.text: Not so the letters of the intellect in the essence, which are counted with the essence. And yet **it looks like the same like *levush*, it's hard to tell the difference**, once they exist as something separate from the essence of the idea.

blocks.title: A book cut up with scissors
blocks.text: So what is he saying? Take *Shaar HaYichud*, a book made of letters. Are they *kelim* or *levushim*? Look at the written letters in front of you and you have to say *levushim*: you can take a scissors and cut the book up into little pieces. Yet put them into a different *tziruf* and it is not *Shaar HaYichud* anymore. So with a *Sefer Torah*: its letters are really *levushim*, since you can take an eraser and change one. But change one letter, add one or erase one, and it is not a *Sefer Torah* anymore, because now the *levushim* are not the same as the *kelim*.

blocks.title: Clothes that fit
blocks.text: A *kli* is like an organ and a *levush* like clothing. Try to wear pants on your torso or a shirt on your bottom: it won't fit. A garment has to be the right size, exactly according to the body. And when you move your arm, your sleeve moves too; put somebody in a headlock and what touches him is really your sleeve, not your arm. A *levush* that is not according to the *kli* is not the same thing anymore.

blocks.title: The letters flew up into the air
blocks.text: So which is the *levush* and which the *kelim*? Think of the Torah scroll that was burned, when it was said the letters flew up into the air. You might object: it was smoke that flew up; the letters were destroyed. No: the *levushim* were destroyed, but you cannot destroy the *kelim*. The Torah stays the Torah. If something happened, G-d forbid, to the copy of *Shaar HaYichud* on his table, it would not affect the book *Shaar HaYichud* at all, and *Chumash Bereishis* is still *Chumash Bereishis*. When the Romans burnt the Torah scroll they could burn only the *levushim*. The *kelim* are part of the essence of the idea of the Torah, and they stay.

The main place of *kelim* is *davka* the Torah. *Torah sheb'al peh* (the Oral Torah) is a kind of hybrid: Rashi says it one way, Tosafos another. Even *Shaar HaYichud*: *Etz Chaim* and other books say the same thing differently; this one says it so we can understand. It has its own *kelim*, or it would not be *Shaar HaYichud*, yet it is itself a *levush* to a more inner thought.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 210 opens where 209 stopped, in the middle of the discussion of lines 36-37, before it reads line 38.

blocks.text: It does not *davka* have to be explained this way, even though the book calls itself the key. If you want the key, it does have to be this way, or people won't understand. But the big ones understand without *Shaar HaYichud*, as the Arizal did. Rabbi Markel would not be surprised if Eliyahu HaNavi, or whoever came to the Arizal, slipped him a *Shaar HaYichud*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 210 opens where 209 stopped, in the middle of the discussion of lines 36-37, before it reads line 38.

blocks.text: The Written Torah has to be *davka* in those letters. In *Torah sheb'al peh* there can be different ways and both are Torah, *eilu v'eilu divrei Elokim chaim* (these and these are the words of the living G-d), though the *tzirufim* changed; in the Written Torah that is the *etzem* itself. Yet even there are *levushim*: the Roman, Apostomos he thinks, could burn the scroll, but the letters flew up; the *kelim* are still there. So *Shaar HaYichud* is made up *davka* of these letters; change them and it is another book.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 210 opens where 209 stopped, in the middle of the discussion of lines 36-37, before it reads line 38.

blocks.text: What about the explanations this series wrote on it? Explanations are explanations; *Shaar HaYichud* is *Shaar HaYichud*, and the explanation is "the new, improved *Kabbala* series", or whatever you want to call it: additions. An edition all in Hebrew that sets out the original shows that these explanations are *levushim* for the *kelim* of the actual book. And yet once an explanation has been revealed in a certain way, that's it.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 210 opens where 209 stopped, in the middle of the discussion of lines 36-37, before it reads line 38.

blocks.text: That is why the series was put out with a copyright: you may disseminate it, but you may not change anything, because if they change something they change an idea. In some places, where it says there is a G-d, all you have to do is put the letters n-o in there and it means exactly the opposite.

sections.title: Both are true, and the whole book depends on it
sections.summary: In their root in the Essence the letters are vessels, one with it, and they also become garments wholly separate from it, because their root is higher than light. On this turn the levels of the worlds, the *kelipos*, free choice and *Tohu*, and the whole book.

phrases.he: ונמצא מובן דשניהם אמת
phrases.en: And we see that they're both true.

phrases.he: בשרש בחינת האותיות
phrases.en: And this goes all the way to the *shoresh* in the *Atzmus*.

phrases.he: דלפעמים הם בבחינת כלים בהיותם בשרש מחצבם באחדות גמור עם העצם, כנזכר לעיל
וגם הם נעשים בבחינת לבושים נפרדים מן העצם לגמרי, כנזכר לעיל
(להיות כי שרש האותיות מבחינת המקיפים, שהן שרש הלבושים ומשם גם כן שרש בכלים המגבילים ומתארים כו' כנזכר לעיל, וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר)

blocks.text: **We see that they're both true**, and **this goes all the way to the *shoresh* in the *Atzmus***: there too are *kelim* and *levushim*. That letters can be wholly separate is itself because they come from the Essence, higher than a light. A light separated from its source stops existing; the letters' root is higher, so even separate they go on existing.

phrases.he: ובכל זה יובן למשכיל למעלה דרך כלל בכל בחינת לבושין דמחשבה דבור ומעשה, ג' מיני אותיות בכל פרטי העשר ספירות בהשתלשלות עד רום המעלות בעצמות אור אין סוף, באותיות דגליף גליפו בטהירו עילאה וכהאי גוונא, ודי למבין:

blocks.text: So with the three kinds of letters, thought, speech and action, up to the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* (the infinite light). As it says, *levushin tekinas lon d'minayhu parchin nishmasin livnei nasha*: a garment of a higher level can be the soul of a lower one, as *Malchus* above becomes *Keser* below. From the Rebbe's words comes the *chassid*'s will and the inner light of his intellect. To us *Adam Kadmon* is *Adam Kadmon*, a listener adds, but to what is higher it is a *levush*. Yes, and it keeps going.

This book is a perfect example. It is a magical book, always an example on itself: if you wonder what example to use, use the book. The book in front of us is *davka* *levushim*, not *kelim*: the *levushim* hold the *kelim*, and the *kelim* hold the light of the intellect. And yet these garments of a physical book become, to us, the inner light of our own intellect.

So too the inner name and the outer name. The inner name is a *kli*, and more: the *etzem* comes from it, from the name of what it is, because the name describes what it is. Upstairs the same: to want the *ratzon hapashut*, you had to say the name *ratzon hapashut*. Then the outer name becomes *kelim* and *levushim* again.

This is how a separate world can come into being at all. The separation of the world from the *Atzmus* comes from the fact that *kelim* can turn into *levushim* and separate out. Free choice, the *yetzer hara* (the evil inclination), *Tohu* (the world of Chaos) and *Tikkun* (the world of Repair) all depend on it: *Tohu* is when the letters get mixed up. The letters that are *kelim* cannot get mixed up.

Explain something to somebody, and he takes it and mixes it up until it comes out like the email a listener was talking about: G-d is one and G-d's will is the main thing, so you can do whatever you like.

All the matters of the book, from chapter one to the end, depend on this: the letters as *kelim* and as *levushim*. It is the main thing of the whole *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent), which goes down through the letters.

This is how *Atzilus*, and *Adam Kadmon*, can be called *Beriya*, a whole new thing. Towards the *Atzmus*, *Adam Kadmon*, *Atik* and *Atzilus* are called *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, separate worlds; towards *Atzilus*, *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya* are the separate worlds; and towards *Malchus* of *Asiya* comes the world of the *kelipos*, a totally separate world. The *chashmal* (literally, electrum) is this too: the *kelim* turn into *levushim*, and then the *levushim* are a *kelipa*.

blocks.title: The peanut shell and the banana peel
blocks.text: What is a *kelipa*? The outside of the letters peels off. It is a husk, like the shell of a peanut or a banana peel, which comes off. When the outer peel of the letter comes off, it becomes a *levush* that is not connected. There is a garment that is connected, while a person is wearing it, and a garment that is not.
This is a very, very important concept, because the whole book depends on it. Understand it and you understand *yichuda tata'a* (the lower unity) better than all the books explain it.

blocks.title: The sar of a nation
blocks.text: Without knowing the names of the demons and the angels and all that, if you understand the letters you can see how they are in people's brains, separate letters that can turn over into other letters. That is what the *sarim* (the princes of the nations) are about. The *sar* of a country is its letters, its *nefesh*, its *ratzon*: the *sar* of America went against the *sar* of Iraq. And you can see them. There is a *sar* of France: a national identity, a *ratzon* and what they are all about, as in America with football and in Mexico with the bullfighting. A listener calls it the daemon; no, a daemon is personal, of an individual, the *shedim* (demons). The genius of a whole nation is higher: those are the seventy *sarim*.

blocks.title: Sarim and shedim
blocks.text: The *shedim* have kings too, but the *sarim* are higher than the demons: they are the *koach hamaskil* of *kelipa*, while the demons have three levels, *Chabad*, *Chagas* and *Nehi* (intellect, emotions and their reactions), whether Jewish demons or gentile ones. It is not like people think.
The way people learn this whole thing, it's a bunch of baloney: they don't understand what a demon or a genius is, or anything like that.

sensitivity.reason: Calls the way others learn about demons and the princes of the nations "a bunch of baloney".
sensitivity.publishable: The way people learn this whole thing, they don't understand what a demon or a genius is, or anything like that.

blocks.text: Understand these matters of *Shaar HaYichud* and you can *mamash* see the demon and the *sar*. It is like the national psyche, as a listener put it, but higher than a psyche: the inner *ratzon*, the *koach hamaskil*, up to the actual *etzem haratzon* (essence of the will) of the country. That is what *Moshiach* will compel, the seventy *sarim*, because he is from higher than them, and the compulsion will take place *davka* through *Shaar HaYichud*.

reviewQuestions.question: Why are the letters of an idea counted with its essence even though they limit and define it?
Why is a pot a poor picture of a *kli*, and what is a better one?
How does the same example, two commentators explaining one idea, show both that the letters are *kelim* and that they are *levushim*?
What does a man who sits and worries show about the letters of thought?
Can you cut up or burn the letters of *Shaar HaYichud* or a *Sefer Torah*? What survives, and why does changing one letter matter?
Why can letters exist separate from the essence when a light cannot?
